rejected.title: Locke and Latham's goal-setting theory
card: Locke and Latham said that clear goals drive effort and performance. A goal gives a worker a target to aim at and a way to judge their own progress.
Clarity and challenge
A goal should be specific, so the worker knows what to do. It should also be hard enough to stretch the worker, but not so hard that it seems out of reach.
Commitment and feedback
Workers need to accept the goal and care about reaching it. Feedback on progress lets them see how they are going and adjust their effort.
Task complexity
For a complex task, the goal needs more time and support, so workers are not overwhelmed. A worker can then learn and plan as they go.
rejected.remember: Motivating goals are clear, challenging, accepted, tracked with feedback and matched to the task.

a.q: Which goal for a sales team best shows the clarity part of goal-setting theory?
opts: Sell 40 new phone plans by the end of March
Try to do better than last quarter at selling
Aim to be the best sales team you can be
Work hard to bring in as many sales as possible
a.why: A goal of 40 plans by the end of March is specific, so staff know exactly what to aim for. The other options are vague, so workers cannot tell what to do or when they have reached the goal.
a.clue: Which goal tells staff exactly what to achieve and by when?

b.q: Priya manages a bakery in Geelong. She sets each baker a target of 300 loaves a day, up from 120, and posts each baker's daily count on a board. Staff say the target is impossible. Which part of the theory is most clearly missing?
opts: A goal that is challenging but seems reachable
A goal that is specific enough to be measured
Feedback given to staff on how they are tracking
A goal with extra time and support for complexity
b.why: The target is a specific number, and the daily board shows each baker how they are going, so clarity and feedback are in place. Feedback is the tempting answer, but the board already gives it. What is missing is a fair challenge: a goal should stretch workers without seeming out of reach, and staff see this one as impossible.
b.clue: The target is clear and tracked, but do the bakers believe they can reach it?

a.q: Which goal for a phone shop sales team is specific and also suitably challenging?
opts: Sell 45 plans a week, up from the usual 35
Sell 35 plans a week, as the team usually does
Sell 120 plans a week, up from the usual 35
Sell more plans each week than before
a.why: A rise from 35 to 45 is specific and stretches staff without being out of reach. The goal of 35 is specific but gives no stretch. The goal of 120 is specific but far too hard, and the last option is not specific.
a.clue: A goal can be specific and still be too easy or too hard.
